server-store.backupFailed: The backup before upgrading the database structure (version {from} → version {to}) could not be written: {error}. Nothing was upgraded, and the database was not changed. Check the space and permissions of the disk {backups} is on, then start again.
server-store.legacyDatabase: The data directory {dir} holds an old-format database ({file}). An old-format database is not imported, and {product} does not change it. Use a new data directory: point DAISY_DATA to a new empty directory, or leave it unset (the system's usual default location), then start again; the old directory can stay as a read-only archive.
server-store.lock.held: This data directory ({dir}) already has a {product} running (process {pid}, started {at}). Only one {product} can run on a data directory at a time: stop it first ({command} stop, or end process {pid}), or use DAISY_DATA to choose another data directory.
server-store.lock.unavailable: Cannot take the data directory's lock {file}: make sure no other {product} is starting, then try again.
server-store.notDaisy: {file} is not a {product} database (perhaps an old-format database renamed, or another program's file). An old-format database is not imported, and {product} does not change it. Use a new data directory: point DAISY_DATA to a new empty directory, or leave it unset (the default location), then start again.
server-store.tooNew: The database {file} has structure version {from}, and the changes of version {need} cannot be used by older code; this {product} only knows up to version {target}. The database was not changed. What to do: go back to the newer {product}; or stop {product}, replace {name} with the backup in {backups} taken before the upgrade to version {need} (the structure version is in the file name), and delete {name}-wal and {name}-shm beside it — data written after the backup is lost.
server-store.unopenable: Cannot open the database {file} ({error}). {product} did not change it. Make sure it is a {product} database and no other program holds it; if it is an old-format database, use a new data directory (set DAISY_DATA).
server-store.unreadable: Cannot read the database {file} ({error}). {product} did not change it. Check its permissions; if it is an old-format database, use a new data directory (set DAISY_DATA).
server-store.updateBackupFailed: The database backup before the update could not be written: {error}. Nothing was updated. Check the space and permissions of the disk {backups} is on.
server-store.upgrade.head: Upgrading the database structure from version {from} to version {to} failed: step {step} ({note}) failed: {error}.
server-store.upgrade.newFailed: {head} The new database could not be created: delete {file} and start again, and report this message to the maintainers.
server-store.upgrade.restoreFailed: {head} Undoing it failed too ({error}). Stop {product}, replace {file} with the backup {backup}, and delete the {name}-wal and {name}-shm files beside it. {what}
server-store.upgrade.restored: {head} The transaction could not be fully rolled back, so the backup taken before the upgrade was restored: the database is back at version {from} (no data was written after the backup). {where}{what}
server-store.upgrade.rolledBack: {head} It was rolled back: the whole upgrade ran in one transaction and was undone; the database is still at version {from} and its structure was not changed (every write of this upgrade was undone). {what}
server-store.upgrade.what: {product} does not start. What to do: go back to the previous {product} (after an automatic update the start guard switches back by itself) and report this message to the maintainers; do not restart again and again until it is fixed.
server-store.upgrade.where: The backup taken before the upgrade is at {backup}.
